english.title: Distribute an image / sound recording which was threatening intending to stir up religious / sexual orientation hatred
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) distributed a recording of visual images or sounds, namely **(..SPECIFY THE RECORDING..), which were threatening, intending thereby to stir up

(A)_[religious hatred]_
(B)_[hatred on the grounds of sexual orientation]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 29E(1) and 29L(3) of the Public Order Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
distributed a recording of visual images/sounds which were threatening
intending to stir up religious hatred / hatred on the grounds of sexual orientation

english.notes:
(i) Section 29E(2) of the Public Order Act 1986 provides that recording means any record from which visual images or sounds may, by any means, be reproduced; and references to the distribution of a recording are to its distribution to the public or a section of the public.
(ii) The consent of the Attorney General is required for prosecution of this offence.
(iii) See also H8427 'show/play recording of threatening images/sounds intending to stir up religious hatred'.
(iv) Section 29L(2) of the Public Order Act 1986 provides that for purposes of the rules against charging more than one offence in the same count or information, each of sections 29B to 29G creates one offence.
(v) This offence was inserted into the Public Order Act 1986 by the Racial and Religious Hatred Act 2006 and amended to include "hatred on the grounds of sexual orientation" as from 23/03/2010 by Sch 16 to the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Note:
Until the introduction of section 154 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to Twelve months is to be read as six months.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
